questions.approvalNote: Science concept, answer key, chapter/competency mapping, marking and question format checked. Teacher moderation is recommended before high-stakes use.
questions.stimulus: A student places a clean magnesium strip into aqueous copper sulphate. After some time, a reddish-brown deposit forms and the blue solution becomes paler.

parts.prompt: Name the type of reaction taking place.
parts.answerKey: A displacement reaction, or no reaction where the metal is less reactive than the displaced metal.

parts.prompt: Name the metal deposited, if any.
parts.answerKey: copper.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced equation and explain the result using the reactivity series.
parts.answerKey: Mg + CuSO₄ → MgSO₄ + Cu. The observation is explained because magnesium is more reactive than copper.

answerKey.modelAnswer:
(a) A displacement reaction, or no reaction where the metal is less reactive than the displaced metal.
(b) copper.
(c) Mg + CuSO₄ → MgSO₄ + Cu. The observation is explained because magnesium is more reactive than copper.

alternatives.prompt: A student places an iron nail in copper sulphate solution. Predict the observation, write the balanced equation and explain the reactivity-based reason.

answerKey.modelAnswer: A reddish-brown copper coating forms on the iron nail and the blue solution becomes greenish. Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces it from solution.

parts.prompt: Identify one observation indicating chemical change.
parts.answerKey: a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms.

parts.prompt: Name the reaction type.
parts.answerKey: It is a precipitation reaction.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced chemical equation.
parts.answerKey: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl.

parts.prompt: Explain why the observation supports the reaction classification.
parts.answerKey: The observation is consistent with formation of new substances in a precipitation reaction; the balanced equation represents conservation of atoms.

answerKey.modelAnswer:
(a) a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms.
(b) It is a precipitation reaction.
(c) Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl.
(d) The observation is consistent with formation of new substances in a precipitation reaction; the balanced equation represents conservation of atoms.

alternatives.prompt: A student burns a magnesium ribbon in air. Describe the observation, write the balanced equation, classify the reaction and explain the mass change.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame and forms white magnesium oxide: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. It is a combination and oxidation reaction. The product contains oxygen from air, so its mass exceeds the original magnesium mass.

markingScheme.criterion: Explain the mass increase using oxygen.

alternatives.prompt: Explain how the human eye focuses light and compare the correction of myopia and hypermetropia.

answerKey.modelAnswer: The cornea and crystalline lens refract light to form an image on the retina. Myopia is corrected using a concave lens, which diverges incoming rays; hypermetropia is corrected using a convex lens, which converges rays before they enter the eye.
